claim: Fetal Leydig cells formed in Nr2f2 mutant testes have reduced steroidogenic function.
source: These observations suggest that FLC formed in the mutant testes have reduced steroidogenic function.
evidence: Inferred from the reduced steroidogenic gene expression normalized to FLC number in mutants.

claim: HSD3B positive fetal Leydig cells present in Nr5a1-Cre; Nr2f2flox/flox mutants are smaller than those in control littermates.
source: HSD3B positive FLC present in Nr5a1-Cre; Nr2f2flox/flox and in Wt1CreERT2; Nr2f2flox/flox mutants were smaller and more elongated than those in control littermates (Figure 5C–H, Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Directly quantified from immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5C-H and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: HSD3B positive fetal Leydig cells present in Nr5a1-Cre; Nr2f2flox/flox mutants are more elongated than those in control littermates.

evidence: Directly quantified from immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5C-H and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

evidence: Directly quantified from immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5C-H and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Small size and elongated shape are cellular characteristics associated with immature fetal Leydig cells at the initial stages of differentiation.
source: These cellular characteristics have been associated with immature FLC at the initial stages of FLC differentiation before the formation of large and round testosterone-producing FLC (van den Driesche et al., 2012; Haider, 2004).
evidence: Supported by citations (van den Driesche et al., 2012; Haider, 2004).

claim: NR2F2 is required in interstitial steroidogenic progenitor cells for initiation of fetal Leydig cell differentiation.
source: Taken together, our results show that NR2F2 is required in interstitial steroidogenic progenitor cells for initiation of FLC differentiation but also for the subsequent step of FLC maturation leading to robust steroid production (Figure 5I).
evidence: Inferred from the reduced NR5A1 upregulation and reduced FLC numbers in mutants.

claim: NR2F2 is required for fetal Leydig cell maturation leading to robust steroid production.
source: Taken together, our results show that NR2F2 is required in interstitial steroidogenic progenitor cells for initiation of FLC differentiation but also for the subsequent step of FLC maturation leading to robust steroid production (Figure 5I).
evidence: Inferred from the reduced steroidogenic gene expression per FLC and the immature morphology of FLC in mutants.

claim: NR2F2 protein is expressed in interstitial cells of coelomic epithelium origin.
source: NR2F2 protein is expressed in interstitial cells of coelomic epithelium and mesonephric origin and is absent or detected at very low levels in FLC as soon as they are formed at E12.5.
evidence: Summarizes findings from immunofluorescence data presented in Figure 1.

claim: NR2F2 protein is expressed in interstitial cells of mesonephric origin.
source: NR2F2 protein is expressed in interstitial cells of coelomic epithelium and mesonephric origin and is absent or detected at very low levels in FLC as soon as they are formed at E12.5.
evidence: Summarizes findings from immunofluorescence data presented in Figure 1.

claim: NR2F2 is absent or detected at very low levels in fetal Leydig cells as soon as they are formed at E12.5.
source: NR2F2 protein is expressed in interstitial cells of coelomic epithelium and mesonephric origin and is absent or detected at very low levels in FLC as soon as they are formed at E12.5.
evidence: Summarizes findings from immunofluorescence data presented in Figure 1.

claim: NR2F2 positive cells are progenitors for fetal Leydig cells.
source: Our observations are consistent with NR2F2 positive cells being progenitors for FLC (Inoue et al., 2016; Ademi et al., 2022; Estermann et al., 2025) and indicate that NR2F2 is quickly downregulated upon differentiation of the fetal steroidogenic lineage, when the cells begin to synthesize steroid hormones.
evidence: Inferred from the expression pattern of NR2F2 and supported by citations (Inoue et al., 2016; Ademi et al., 2022; Estermann et al., 2025).

claim: NR2F2 is quickly downregulated upon differentiation of the fetal steroidogenic lineage.
source: Our observations are consistent with NR2F2 positive cells being progenitors for FLC (Inoue et al., 2016; Ademi et al., 2022; Estermann et al., 2025) and indicate that NR2F2 is quickly downregulated upon differentiation of the fetal steroidogenic lineage, when the cells begin to synthesize steroid hormones.
evidence: Inferred from the absence of NR2F2 in HSD3B+ FLC at E12.5.

claim: Nr2f2 mutants exhibit reduced fetal Leydig cell numbers.
source: We used two Cre lines to address the role of NR2F2 in the mouse fetal testis. Nr2f2 mutants exhibit reduced FLC numbers together with a strong reduction in Insl3 and steroidogenic gene expression, resulting in cryptorchidism and reduced anogenital distance.
evidence: Directly observed in immunofluorescence data from both Wt1CreERT2 and Nr5a1-Cre mutants.

claim: Nr2f2 mutants exhibit a strong reduction in Insl3 expression.
source: We used two Cre lines to address the role of NR2F2 in the mouse fetal testis. Nr2f2 mutants exhibit reduced FLC numbers together with a strong reduction in Insl3 and steroidogenic gene expression, resulting in cryptorchidism and reduced anogenital distance.
evidence: Directly measured by RT-qPCR in both Wt1CreERT2 and Nr5a1-Cre mutants.

claim: Nr2f2 mutants exhibit a strong reduction in steroidogenic gene expression.
source: We used two Cre lines to address the role of NR2F2 in the mouse fetal testis. Nr2f2 mutants exhibit reduced FLC numbers together with a strong reduction in Insl3 and steroidogenic gene expression, resulting in cryptorchidism and reduced anogenital distance.
evidence: Directly measured by RT-qPCR in both Wt1CreERT2 and Nr5a1-Cre mutants.

claim: Nr2f2 mutants exhibit cryptorchidism.
source: We used two Cre lines to address the role of NR2F2 in the mouse fetal testis. Nr2f2 mutants exhibit reduced FLC numbers together with a strong reduction in Insl3 and steroidogenic gene expression, resulting in cryptorchidism and reduced anogenital distance.
evidence: Directly observed in macroscopic images of both Wt1CreERT2 and Nr5a1-Cre mutants.

claim: Nr2f2 mutants exhibit reduced anogenital distance.
source: We used two Cre lines to address the role of NR2F2 in the mouse fetal testis. Nr2f2 mutants exhibit reduced FLC numbers together with a strong reduction in Insl3 and steroidogenic gene expression, resulting in cryptorchidism and reduced anogenital distance.
evidence: Directly measured in Nr5a1-Cre mutants.

claim: The reduction of Insl3 expression is sufficient to impair testis descent even when a fraction of fetal Leydig cells is still present.
source: Importantly, the reduction of Insl3 expression is sufficient to impair testis descent even when a fraction of FLC is still present.
evidence: Inferred from the cryptorchidism phenotype in Nr5a1-Cre mutants where some FLC are still present.

claim: NR2F2 is an essential regulator of fetal Leydig cell development in the mouse.
source: Our findings identify NR2F2 as an essential regulator of FLC and male reproductive system development in the mouse.
evidence: Inferred from the FLC phenotype in Nr2f2 mutants.

claim: NR2F2 is an essential regulator of male reproductive system development in the mouse.
source: Our findings identify NR2F2 as an essential regulator of FLC and male reproductive system development in the mouse.
evidence: Inferred from the cryptorchidism and reduced anogenital distance phenotypes in Nr2f2 mutants.

claim: An independent Nr2f2 conditional mutation results in a similar phenotype of fetal Leydig cell hypoplasia, cryptorchidism, and hypospadias.
source: This conclusion is confirmed by an independent Nr2f2 conditional mutation resulting in a similar phenotype of FLC hypoplasia, cryptorchidism, and hypospadias (Estermann et al., 2025).
evidence: Supported by citation (Estermann et al., 2025).

claim: Nr2f2 deletion using Nr5a1-Cre does not impair the survival of the interstitial steroidogenic progenitor population.
source: Nr2f2 deletion using Nr5a1-Cre does not impair the survival or proliferation of the interstitial steroidogenic progenitor population, yet the FLC population is reduced in Nr5a1-Cre; Nr2f2flox/flox mutant testes.
evidence: Directly observed from cell death and proliferation assays in Nr5a1-Cre mutants.

claim: Nr2f2 deletion using Nr5a1-Cre does not impair the proliferation of the interstitial steroidogenic progenitor population.
source: Nr2f2 deletion using Nr5a1-Cre does not impair the survival or proliferation of the interstitial steroidogenic progenitor population, yet the FLC population is reduced in Nr5a1-Cre; Nr2f2flox/flox mutant testes.
evidence: Directly observed from proliferation assays in Nr5a1-Cre mutants.

claim: The expression of NR5A1 is not upregulated in Nr2f2 mutants.
source: We found that the expression of the master regulator of steroidogenic differentiation of NR5A1 is not upregulated in Nr2f2 mutants, which is sufficient to account for the decrease in FLC numbers (Morohashi et al., 2020; Baba et al., 2018; Baba et al., 2014; Shima et al., 2018).
evidence: Directly observed in immunofluorescence data from Nr5a1-Cre mutants, with citations supporting the role of NR5A1.

claim: Lack of NR5A1 upregulation is sufficient to account for the decrease in fetal Leydig cell numbers in Nr2f2 mutants.
source: We found that the expression of the master regulator of steroidogenic differentiation of NR5A1 is not upregulated in Nr2f2 mutants, which is sufficient to account for the decrease in FLC numbers (Morohashi et al., 2020; Baba et al., 2018; Baba et al., 2014; Shima et al., 2018).
evidence: Inferred from the known role of NR5A1 in FLC differentiation supported by citations (Morohashi et al., 2020; Baba et al., 2018; Baba et al., 2014; Shima et al., 2018).

claim: ChIP-seq analysis of whole E14.5 testes has identified NR2F2 binding peaks in the regulatory region of Nr5a1.
source: ChIP-seq analysis of whole E14.5 testes has identified NR2F2 binding peaks in the regulatory region of Nr5a1 (Estermann et al., 2025).
evidence: Supported by citation (Estermann et al., 2025).

claim: NR2F2 regulates gene expression by directly interacting with NR5A1 in MA-10 cells.
source: In addition, NR2F2 regulates gene expression by directly interacting with NR5A1 in MA-10 cells, an in vitro model for immature ALCs (Mendoza-Villarroel et al., 2014b; Mendoza-Villarroel et al., 2014a; Di-Luoffo et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by citations (Mendoza-Villarroel et al., 2014b; Mendoza-Villarroel et al., 2014a; Di-Luoffo et al., 2022).

claim: A fraction of fetal Leydig cells differentiates in Nr2f2 mutants.
source: A fraction of FLC differentiates in Nr2f2 mutants, including when progenitors of both coelomic epithelium and mesonephric origins are targeted.
evidence: Directly observed in immunofluorescence data from both Wt1CreERT2 and Nr5a1-Cre mutants.

claim: Additional factors cooperate with NR2F2 to regulate the transition from the steroidogenic progenitor state to the differentiating fetal Leydig cell.
source: This observation indicates that additional factors cooperate with NR2F2 to regulate the transition from the steroidogenic progenitor state to the differentiating FLC.
evidence: Inferred from the observation that some FLC still differentiate in the absence of NR2F2.

claim: ARX is a candidate factor that cooperates with NR2F2 to regulate the transition from steroidogenic progenitor to differentiating fetal Leydig cell.
source: The homeodomain protein ARX is expressed in Nr2f2 mutant steroidogenic progenitors and is a good candidate to be such a factor. Arx mutants exhibit decreased FLC numbers without defects in paracrine signals driving their differentiation, similar to Nr2f2 mutants (Miyabayashi et al., 2013).
evidence: Inferred from the similar phenotype of Arx mutants and the expression of ARX in Nr2f2 mutant progenitors, with citation supporting the Arx mutant phenotype.

claim: Fetal Leydig cells and adult Leydig cells are morphologically, transcriptionally, and functionally distinct.
source: FLC and ALC are morphologically, transcriptionally, and functionally distinct (Shima, 2019; Sararols et al., 2021), yet NR2F2 function is required for the differentiation of both lineages.
evidence: Supported by citations (Shima, 2019; Sararols et al., 2021).

claim: NR2F2 function is required for the differentiation of both fetal and adult Leydig cell lineages.
source: FLC and ALC are morphologically, transcriptionally, and functionally distinct (Shima, 2019; Sararols et al., 2021), yet NR2F2 function is required for the differentiation of both lineages.
evidence: Inferred from the current study on FLC and prior work on ALC.

claim: NR2F2 is maintained in cells that have started to express steroidogenesis genes in the postnatal testis.
source: In contrast to the situation in the fetal testis, NR2F2 is maintained in cells that have started to express steroidogenesis genes in the postnatal testis (Inoue et al., 2016; Ademi et al., 2022; Mendoza-Villarroel et al., 2014b).
evidence: Supported by citations (Inoue et al., 2016; Ademi et al., 2022; Mendoza-Villarroel et al., 2014b).

claim: NR2F2 regulates the transition from the adult progenitor Leydig cell to the immature adult Leydig cell.
source: NR2F2 regulates the transition from the adult progenitor Leydig cell (characterized by their elongated shape, their ability to proliferate, and a low level of testosterone synthesis) to the immature ALC (characterized by their round shape, low mitotic activity, and increased testosterone production) (Qin et al., 2008; Haider, 2004).
evidence: Supported by citations (Qin et al., 2008; Haider, 2004).

claim: NR2F2 cooperates with NR5A1 and GATA4 to activate the transcription of Insl3 in MA-10 cells.
source: In agreement with its in vivo role promoting maturation along the ALC lineage, NR2F2 cooperates with NR5A1 and GATA4 to activate the transcription of Insl3, Star (encoding the cholesterol transporter), and Amhr2 (Mendoza-Villarroel et al., 2014b; Mendoza-Villarroel et al., 2014a; Di-Luoffo et al., 2022; Mehanovic et al., 2021; Mehanovic et al., 2022) in MA-10 cells.
evidence: Supported by citations (Mendoza-Villarroel et al., 2014b; Mendoza-Villarroel et al., 2014a; Di-Luoffo et al., 2022; Mehanovic et al., 2021; Mehanovic et al., 2022).

claim: NR2F2 cooperates with NR5A1 and GATA4 to activate the transcription of Star in MA-10 cells.
source: In agreement with its in vivo role promoting maturation along the ALC lineage, NR2F2 cooperates with NR5A1 and GATA4 to activate the transcription of Insl3, Star (encoding the cholesterol transporter), and Amhr2 (Mendoza-Villarroel et al., 2014b; Mendoza-Villarroel et al., 2014a; Di-Luoffo et al., 2022; Mehanovic et al., 2021; Mehanovic et al., 2022) in MA-10 cells.
evidence: Supported by citations (Mendoza-Villarroel et al., 2014b; Mendoza-Villarroel et al., 2014a; Di-Luoffo et al., 2022; Mehanovic et al., 2021; Mehanovic et al., 2022).

claim: NR2F2 cooperates with NR5A1 and GATA4 to activate the transcription of Amhr2 in MA-10 cells.
source: In agreement with its in vivo role promoting maturation along the ALC lineage, NR2F2 cooperates with NR5A1 and GATA4 to activate the transcription of Insl3, Star (encoding the cholesterol transporter), and Amhr2 (Mendoza-Villarroel et al., 2014b; Mendoza-Villarroel et al., 2014a; Di-Luoffo et al., 2022; Mehanovic et al., 2021; Mehanovic et al., 2022) in MA-10 cells.
evidence: Supported by citations (Mendoza-Villarroel et al., 2014b; Mendoza-Villarroel et al., 2014a; Di-Luoffo et al., 2022; Mehanovic et al., 2021; Mehanovic et al., 2022).

claim: The steroidogenic cells that differentiate in Nr2f2 mutant fetal testes exhibit a small size.
source: Here, we found that the steroidogenic cells that differentiate in Nr2f2 mutant fetal testes exhibit a small size, an elongated shape, and reduced steroidogenic gene expression, features of the earliest stages of FLC differentiation (Wen et al., 2016; van den Driesche et al., 2012; Haider, 2004).
evidence: Directly observed in immunofluorescence data from Nr2f2 mutants, with citations supporting the interpretation.

claim: The steroidogenic cells that differentiate in Nr2f2 mutant fetal testes exhibit an elongated shape.
source: Here, we found that the steroidogenic cells that differentiate in Nr2f2 mutant fetal testes exhibit a small size, an elongated shape, and reduced steroidogenic gene expression, features of the earliest stages of FLC differentiation (Wen et al., 2016; van den Driesche et al., 2012; Haider, 2004).
evidence: Directly observed in immunofluorescence data from Nr2f2 mutants, with citations supporting the interpretation.

claim: The steroidogenic cells that differentiate in Nr2f2 mutant fetal testes exhibit reduced steroidogenic gene expression.
source: Here, we found that the steroidogenic cells that differentiate in Nr2f2 mutant fetal testes exhibit a small size, an elongated shape, and reduced steroidogenic gene expression, features of the earliest stages of FLC differentiation (Wen et al., 2016; van den Driesche et al., 2012; Haider, 2004).
evidence: Directly measured by RT-qPCR normalized to FLC number in Nr2f2 mutants, with citations supporting the interpretation.

claim: A similar phenotype is obtained when Nr5a1 is deleted after the onset of fetal Leydig cell differentiation.
source: A similar phenotype is obtained when Nr5a1 is deleted after the onset of FLC differentiation (Buaas et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citation (Buaas et al., 2012).

claim: NR2F2 promotes fetal Leydig cell maturation possibly by directly regulating the initial expression of genes involved in steroidogenesis.
source: This suggests that in addition to controlling the initial engagement of steroidogenic progenitors into the FLC lineage and similar to the situation in the postnatal testis, NR2F2 promotes FLC maturation possibly by directly regulating the initial expression of genes involved in steroidogenesis.
evidence: Inferred from the reduced steroidogenic gene expression per FLC in mutants and the known role of NR2F2 in ALC maturation.

claim: NR2F2 binding peaks are found in the regulatory regions of genes involved in lipid metabolism and cholesterol biosynthesis in ChIP-seq analysis of whole E14.5 testes.
source: In agreement with this hypothesis, NR2F2 binding peaks are found in the regulatory regions of genes involved in lipid metabolism and cholesterol biosynthesis in ChIP-seq analysis of whole E14.5 testes (Estermann et al., 2025).
evidence: Supported by citation (Estermann et al., 2025).

claim: NR2F2 is required for additional aspects of fetal testis morphogenesis and differentiation.
source: NR2F2 is required for additional aspects of fetal testis morphogenesis and differentiation.
evidence: Inferred from the observed testis cord and tunica/PTM defects in mutants.

claim: Testis cords are enlarged and abnormally shaped in Nr2f2 mutants.
source: Testis cords are enlarged and abnormally shaped in Nr2f2 mutants.
evidence: Directly observed in immunofluorescence data from Wt1CreERT2 mutants.

claim: Testis cord development involves the formation of Sertoli-germ cell masses after E11.5.
source: Testis cord development involves the formation of Sertoli-germ cell masses after E11.5 and their subsequent partition by growing wedges of interstitial cells and associated vascular branches at E12.5 (Cool et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citation (Cool et al., 2012).

claim: Testis cord development involves partition of Sertoli-germ cell masses by growing wedges of interstitial cells and associated vascular branches at E12.5.
source: Testis cord development involves the formation of Sertoli-germ cell masses after E11.5 and their subsequent partition by growing wedges of interstitial cells and associated vascular branches at E12.5 (Cool et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citation (Cool et al., 2012).

claim: Pathogenic variants in NR2F2 have been associated with congenital heart disease.
source: Pathogenic variants in NR2F2 have been associated with congenital malformations, including congenital heart disease, congenital diaphragmatic hernia, and syndromic 46,XX testicular or ovo-testicular difference/disorder in sex development (DSD) (Polvani et al., 2019; Bashamboo et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations (Polvani et al., 2019; Bashamboo et al., 2018).

claim: Pathogenic variants in NR2F2 have been associated with congenital diaphragmatic hernia.
source: Pathogenic variants in NR2F2 have been associated with congenital malformations, including congenital heart disease, congenital diaphragmatic hernia, and syndromic 46,XX testicular or ovo-testicular difference/disorder in sex development (DSD) (Polvani et al., 2019; Bashamboo et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations (Polvani et al., 2019; Bashamboo et al., 2018).

claim: Pathogenic variants in NR2F2 have been associated with syndromic 46,XX testicular or ovo-testicular difference/disorder in sex development.
source: Pathogenic variants in NR2F2 have been associated with congenital malformations, including congenital heart disease, congenital diaphragmatic hernia, and syndromic 46,XX testicular or ovo-testicular difference/disorder in sex development (DSD) (Polvani et al., 2019; Bashamboo et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations (Polvani et al., 2019; Bashamboo et al., 2018).

claim: Defects in the external genitalia (micropenis, hypospadias) have been associated with rare heterozygous variants in NR2F2 in 46,XY patients.
source: More recently, defects in the external genitalia (micropenis, hypospadias) and cryptorchidism have been associated with rare heterozygous variants in NR2F2 in 46,XY patients (Zidoune et al., 2022; Ganapathi et al., 2023; Wankanit et al., 2024).
evidence: Supported by citations (Zidoune et al., 2022; Ganapathi et al., 2023; Wankanit et al., 2024).

claim: Cryptorchidism has been associated with rare heterozygous variants in NR2F2 in 46,XY patients.
source: More recently, defects in the external genitalia (micropenis, hypospadias) and cryptorchidism have been associated with rare heterozygous variants in NR2F2 in 46,XY patients (Zidoune et al., 2022; Ganapathi et al., 2023; Wankanit et al., 2024).
evidence: Supported by citations (Zidoune et al., 2022; Ganapathi et al., 2023; Wankanit et al., 2024).

claim: Defects in external genitalia and cryptorchidism in 46,XY patients can be attributed to defects in testosterone-dependent masculinization and INSL3-dependent testis descent during gestation.
source: These phenotypes can be attributed to defects in testosterone-dependent masculinization and INSL3-dependent testis descent during gestation and could be explained by a failure of FLC differentiation in the fetal testis.
evidence: Inferred from established knowledge about the roles of testosterone and INSL3 in male development.

claim: Defects in external genitalia and cryptorchidism in 46,XY patients could be explained by a failure of fetal Leydig cell differentiation in the fetal testis.
source: These phenotypes can be attributed to defects in testosterone-dependent masculinization and INSL3-dependent testis descent during gestation and could be explained by a failure of FLC differentiation in the fetal testis.
evidence: Inferred from the role of FLC in producing testosterone and INSL3.

claim: NR2F2 is abundantly expressed in interstitial cells of fetal human testes.
source: NR2F2 is abundantly expressed in interstitial cells of fetal human testes, a population that likely contains the progenitors for FLC (Kilcoyne et al., 2014; van den Driesche et al., 2012; Lottrup et al., 2014; Taelman et al., 2024).
evidence: Supported by citations (Kilcoyne et al., 2014; van den Driesche et al., 2012; Lottrup et al., 2014; Taelman et al., 2024).

claim: Interstitial cells of fetal human testes likely contain the progenitors for fetal Leydig cells.
source: NR2F2 is abundantly expressed in interstitial cells of fetal human testes, a population that likely contains the progenitors for FLC (Kilcoyne et al., 2014; van den Driesche et al., 2012; Lottrup et al., 2014; Taelman et al., 2024).
evidence: Inferred from the expression pattern of NR2F2 and supported by citations (Kilcoyne et al., 2014; van den Driesche et al., 2012; Lottrup et al., 2014; Taelman et al., 2024).

claim: NR2F2 is required in the steroidogenic progenitors of the murine fetal testis for the initiation of fetal Leydig cell differentiation.
source: The present work demonstrating that NR2F2 is required in the steroidogenic progenitors of the murine fetal testis for the initiation and progression of FLC differentiation provides an entry point in understanding the etiology of 46,XY DSD associated with pathogenic NR2F2 variants.
evidence: Summarizes findings from the current study.

claim: NR2F2 is required in the steroidogenic progenitors of the murine fetal testis for the progression of fetal Leydig cell differentiation.
source: The present work demonstrating that NR2F2 is required in the steroidogenic progenitors of the murine fetal testis for the initiation and progression of FLC differentiation provides an entry point in understanding the etiology of 46,XY DSD associated with pathogenic NR2F2 variants.
evidence: Summarizes findings from the current study.

claim: This work provides an entry point in understanding the etiology of 46,XY DSD associated with pathogenic NR2F2 variants.
source: The present work demonstrating that NR2F2 is required in the steroidogenic progenitors of the murine fetal testis for the initiation and progression of FLC differentiation provides an entry point in understanding the etiology of 46,XY DSD associated with pathogenic NR2F2 variants.
evidence: Inferred from the relevance of the mouse findings to human disease.
